ummādantī: [U+mada+ṇe+anta]  CL=7 A woman named Ummādantī. During the era of Lord Buddha Kassapa, she worked for three years to earn a wage sufficient to buy a piece of cloth dyed with red flower dye. She donated this beautifully colored cloth to a monk, a disciple of Lord Buddha, and made the following aspiration: 'If I am to remain in Saṃsāra, may I become the most beautiful woman, such that any man who sees me becomes captivated and loses his senses. As a result of this wish, she was reborn as the daughter of a wealthy merchant possessing eighty billion in wealth in Ariṭṭhapura City, in the Sivi country. She was named Ummādantī because of her beauty, which could enchant anyone who saw her. She eventually became a therī  (a senior nun) named Uppavaṇā. See - Ā, 2. 39-47. Jā,ṭṭha,5.220-240. Apa,2.233. Therī,ṭṭha. 200.
